key_insight: High-rate cavitation can reveal distinct effective degradation histories for viscosity and shear modulus, with reductions occurring at different stages of the event.
engineering_relevance: Time-varying property identification can improve characterization of soft, tissue-like materials under extreme loading relevant to biomechanics and medical engineering.
method: Infer viscoelastic behavior from laser-induced bubble radius–time measurements using Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry.
Represent evolving shear modulus, viscosity, or both with normalized sigmoid histories.
Evaluate recovery on synthetic histories and apply the framework to polyacrylamide and gelatin datasets.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests recovered prescribed constant and evolving properties; experimental datasets showed viscosity decreases throughout, while shear-modulus reductions varied by material and formulation.
watch_item: The inferred histories are effective properties constrained by sigmoid evolution and do not independently distinguish damage, fracture, or plasticity.
paper_title: Soft material mechanical property degradation at high strain rates
